questions: If multiple people have the same maximum score, should they all receive the same rank r, and then r increments by k (the count of those people) for the next group?
Should the output be printed in the order of person labels (1 to N), or in the order determined by the ranking process (e.g., sorted by rank)?
If there are ties in scores that are not the current maximum (e.g., two people with the second-highest score), should they also receive the same rank when their turn comes?
Is the input guaranteed to be on exactly two lines, with the second line containing exactly N integers separated by spaces?
Should the ranks be printed as integers, one per line, without any extra spaces or text?
If N=1, should the rank be printed as 1 (since r starts at 1 and k=1)?
Are the scores P_i guaranteed to be integers within the given range, and if non-integer values are input, should the program handle them or can it assume integer input?
Should the algorithm handle cases where all scores are identical, assigning rank 1 to all N people?
